summary.answer:
**Houston TX ships the most revenue to customers outside its own country in 2023:** about **$139K gross** (2,015 items), or **about $108K net** after removing cancelled and returned items. It's first by both measures.

**How "outside its own country" works here:** all 10 distribution centers are in the US, so this just means sales to customers whose country isn't the United States. I linked each item to a center through the product's assigned center (`products.distribution_center_id`), used the customer's country from `users`, and counted items created in 2023.

| Distribution center | Net foreign revenue | Gross foreign revenue | Foreign share of center's revenue |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Houston TX** | **$108.3K** | **$139.4K** | 78.7% |
| Memphis TN | $86.9K | $116.6K | 78.7% |
| Chicago IL | $86.3K | $117.2K | 78.5% |
| Mobile AL | $79.8K | $101.3K | 77.6% |
| Philadelphia PA | $66.4K | $86.3K | 75.3% |
| … | … | … | … |
| Charleston SC (lowest) | $43.2K | $57.6K | 79.0% |

**Why Houston wins:** it's the biggest center overall ($177K total gross revenue, about 19% more than Chicago or Memphis). Its foreign share (about 79%) is about the same as every other center's (75–79%). So Houston leads because it sells more in total, not because it's more focused on foreign customers. Its lead over Memphis and Chicago (about 25% net) is clear. Memphis and Chicago are essentially tied for second.

**Confidence:** high that Houston ranks first in this dataset. Low that this means anything about real shipping. Caveats:
- **This is synthetic data.** Products are assigned to centers at random, which is why every center's foreign share is about 78%. That matches the customer mix (about 80% of users are outside the US, mainly China and Brazil).
- **There's no actual shipment record.** The center comes from the product's assignment, not from tracking where an order shipped from.
- **Customer country comes from the user's profile address,** not the shipping address on each order.
- **The dataset is regenerated from time to time,** so the exact amounts will shift if you rerun this. The ranking has generally held.
- **Gross vs. net:** gross counts all item sale prices; net leaves out cancelled and returned items. Houston is first either way.

input.sql:
SELECT dc.name,
  ROUND(SUM(IF(oi.status NOT IN ('Cancelled','Returned') AND u.country!='United States', oi.sale_price,0)),0) net_intl_rev,
  ROUND(SUM(IF(u.country!='United States', oi.sale_price,0)),0) gross_intl_rev,
  ROUND(SUM(oi.sale_price),0) gross_total_rev,
  ROUND(SAFE_DIVIDE(SUM(IF(u.country!='United States', oi.sale_price,0)),SUM(oi.sale_price))*100,1) intl_pct,
  COUNTIF(u.country!='United States') intl_items
FROM `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.order_items` oi
JOIN `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.products` p ON p.id=oi.product_id
JOIN `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.distribution_centers` dc ON dc.id=p.distribution_center_id
JOIN `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.users` u ON u.id=oi.user_id
WHERE oi.created_at >= '2023-01-01' AND oi.created_at < '2024-01-01'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY net_intl_rev DESC
